We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene). 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. In our target, the unsaturated acid is attached to an anilide (C=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait target: .../C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So we have an α,β-unsaturated carboxamide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). The amide formation step is forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break that unsaturated acid via Doebner: gives aldehyde (c2ccc)?? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring c2ccc(... )cc2 (the sulfonyl phenyl). The unsaturated acid is attached via the double bond to that phenyl ring: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring at the β carbon (the double bond). So the aldehyde precursor would be the aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). Indeed Doebner uses aromatic aldehyde. So we need aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl group attached? The sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the aldehyde? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the aldehyde carbon? Actually structure: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . So the sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (c2). That phenyl ring also bears the α,β-unsaturated side chain at para position relative to sulfonamide? So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with sulfonamide and aldehyde substituent (instead of the side chain). So we need to generate that aldehyde via Doebner from aromatic aldehyde (same ring) and malonic acid. So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline. Then unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (same ring) + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl chloride + aniline). Actually forward sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the aniline is the phenyl ring with methyl substituent? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the methyl phenyl ring (first phenyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (first ring) which has a methyl substituent. So the sulfonamide formation step: the nitrogen of that first phenyl (aniline) reacts with sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (c2...). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give aniline (first phenyl) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2) with sulfonyl group attached to it (Ar-SO2-Cl). So we need to propose that.

Thus overall three steps:

Step1 (retro amide): target -> precursor A (α,β-unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amide formation uses coupling agent.

Step2 (retro Doebner): precursor A (α,β-unsaturated acid) -> aromatic aldehyde (same phenyl with sulfonyl) + malonic acid.

Step3 (retro sulfonamide): sulfonyl phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (first phenyl with methyl) -> sulfonamide (the sulfonyl phenyl attached to nitrogen). Wait we already used aniline in step1? Actually step1 uses aniline (c3...). That's a different aniline (the second phenyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (methyl phenyl). So step3 should involve that first phenyl (with methyl) as amine, reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl (which also is part of the aldehyde). So after step2 we have aromatic aldehyde (sulfonyl phenyl) and malonic acid. The sulfonyl phenyl is still attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the aldehyde precursor is the phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl group (SO2Cl?) Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring as part of sulfonamide; after breaking sulfonamide we have sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring (Ar-SO2-Cl). The aldehyde is on same ring? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonamide nitrogen. So after breaking sulfonamide, we have Ar-SO2-Cl (where Ar is phenyl with methyl and para side chain). The side chain is the α,β-unsaturated acid (which after step2 becomes aldehyde). So after step2, we have Ar-SO2-Cl with aldehyde substituent (para). So step3: Ar-SO2-Cl + aniline (first phenyl) -> sulfonamide.

Thus we need to produce final route JSON with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have some templates from earlier search: template 733 is sulfonamide formation (Cl-SO2-aryl + aniline -> sulfonamide). That matches our sulfonamide step. Good.

For amide formation, we need a template that forms amide from carboxylic acid and amine via coupling. Search maybe not found earlier. Let's search for amide formation template.
